title: Continuing Your Education
before:
Resources

  • Find Your College. Explore resources, to plan, prepare, and graduate from college. Provided by the National Center for Education Statistics.
  • College Navigator. Find the right college for you by searching more than 7,000 institutions in the United States. Provided by the National Center for Education Statistics.
  • Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). The application process for financial aid is separate from the process of applying for admission to a college or university. The FAFSA is the application for most federal student aid programs (including the Federal Pell Grant Program) and the Maine State Grant Program. If you want to receive any form of financial aid, including loans, you must fill-out the FAFSA.
  • National & Regional Accreditors. Accrediting bodies recognized by the U.S. Secretary of Education or the Council for Higher Education Accreditation.
  • . Provides education planning resources from the U.S. Department of Education.

Maine Resources

  • Specialized Programs. The following specialized programs are not offered by Maine higher education institutions. Financial Authority of Maine (FAME) has made accommodations so that Maine students may qualify for and participate in these programs.
    • Medical Education Program
    • Maine Dental Education Loan & Loan Repayment Program
  • Student Loan Repayment Information. FAME offers guidance throughout the loan repayment process. If you're a teacher, you may qualify for loan forgiveness, loan deferment or forbearance options.

notes: 2 section headers — too few for a contents list.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 2 headings sit at a level the page never opens — "Resources" is an h3 with no h2 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 2 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 4 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

findings.name: list-item-whose-link-is-gone
